minutes.headline: School Committee passed a deeply-cut FY26 budget and created Lunenburg's first student transportation fee.
minutes.summary:
The School Committee worked through the superintendent's FY26 recommended budget line by line, confirming a Director of Finance restructuring, a cut to one of two curriculum coaches, and rejecting a proposed librarian cut, while extensive public comment focused on athletic and band cuts, the co-op ski program's cost, and equity between academics and extracurriculars. The committee voted to table a ski program cut pending renegotiation with partner schools, adopted a new student bus fee (with rates and a waiver policy sent to the policy subcommittee) to help offset transportation costs, and ultimately passed the FY26 budget unanimously with the ski program retained and funded by projected bus fee revenue; members also confirmed they will not pursue a school override this year in favor of a possible townwide override next year.</summary>
</invoke>

what_happened.line: The School Committee passed the superintendent's recommended FY26 budget unanimously, keeping the co-op ski program and funding it with projected bus fee revenue.
The committee adopted a new student transportation fee, sending rates and a waiver policy to the policy subcommittee, on a 4-1 vote.
A proposed cut to the co-op ski program was tabled while the athletic director tries to renegotiate cost-sharing with partner schools.
Following a joint meeting with the Select Board, members reached consensus against a school-specific override this year, favoring a possible townwide override next year.
The committee reached consensus to cut one of two curriculum coach positions and to keep the librarian position.

why_it_matters: A transportation fee is new for Lunenburg families and will need a waiver policy before it takes effect, which the policy subcommittee is now drafting.
The FY26 budget's cuts and restorations -- coaches, band transportation, the ski program -- set what programs the schools run next year without a tax override this year.
Whether a townwide override happens next year is now the mechanism residents should watch for how school funding gets decided going forward.
